work.title: Arcona
Arcona
Ballet i 4 Akter af August Bournonville
Ballet in Four Acts by August Bournonville

annot.p: Article also published in Frederiksborg Amts Avis on 15. May 1875.

history.p: August Bournonville got his inspiration for "Arcona" from the chronicles of the Danish King Valdemar I's victorious crusades against the Rani on the island of Rügen and the capture of the fortress Arcona. Originally it had been the plan, that the ballet was to be performed in connection with the inauguration of the new building of The Royal Theatre on 15 October 1874. However, although Hartmann reused parts of his music from "Liden Kirsten" (HartW 3), and three of the dances were arranged by V.C. Holm and C.C. Møller, it was not finished on time. It therefore lasted almost a year before it was possible to stage a great ballet created specifically for the new theatre.

annot.p: Contains sketches for Acts One and Two of "Arcona" and the songs: "Hroar og Helge paa Vifils Ø" (HartW 437), "Saa mange i Tal de ere" (HartW A 14) from Berthold Auerbachs "I stille Timer" and "Valdemar Atterdag" (Da Kongen, min Fader, i Muld var lagt) (HartW A 15).

physDesc.physMedium: 2 volumes in black cardboard containing drafts for piano with sporadic indication of instrumentation for Acts One and Two and Acts Three and Four. Written in black ink and pencil with additions in blue and red crayon. Vol. 1 paginated 1-96 and vol. 2 1-70, although the last twelve pages ("The Finale") consists of three separate oblong bifolios. Dated on vol. 1 p. 3: "21/6 73"; p. 84: "22/11 73"; vol. 2 p. 46: "26/3 74". On p. 65 in vol. 1 after the first ten bars of No. 5, Hartmann has written: "osv: efter Claveerudtoget til 'liden Kirsten', pag. 68-71." On p. 70 signed and end-dated: "17/4 / I:P:E: Hartmann".

annot.p: The first piano version of the complete music for "Arcona".

physDesc.physMedium: Written in brown ink and pencil. Paper: 12 staves. Paginated in foreign hand 1-34, five pages blank. On the first page, vague sketches in pencil, and added in foreign hand: "J.P.E. Hartmann: 'Arkona' / Skizzer af Arkona. Hartmanns Manuskript." On the first music page: "3die Acts Finale / omcomponeret." At the end of the music on p. 9 dated: "Søllerød / 2/12 74." On p. 10 above the music: "Fjerde Act.", and added in pencil: "Arcona op. 72." Sporadic indications of instrumentation.

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in cardboard with leather spine and marbled sides. Handwritten label pasted on front cover, inscribed: "Arcona / 1ste og 2den Act Partitur." Stamped: DET KGL THEATERS / MUSIKARCHIV. No title page. Written in brown ink with bar-lines in blue crayon. Paper: 20 staves. Various paginations. At the bottom of each page, later pagination in pencil 1-304. The overture signed and end-dated: "I:P:E: Hartmann / 10/4 75." Above the beginning of Act One dated: "Novbr. 1873." At the end of No. 3 on p. 73 Hartmann has written: "NB Herefter følge 3 Dandse med indlagt Musik." Nos. 4 to 6 are not included in this score. At the end of Act One on p. 136 dated: "Fine 16/6 74." At the end of No. 13 Hartmann has written: "her følger Optogsmarschen af "liden Kirsten". At the end of Act Two on p. 304 end-dated: "2/11 74."

Bound in cardboard with leather spine and marbled sides. Handwritten label pasted on front cover, inscribed: "Arcona / 3-4. Act Partitur." Stamped: DET KGL THEATERS / MUSIKARCHIV. No title page. Written in brown ink with bar-lines and emendations in blue crayon. Paper: 20 staves. Various paginations. At the bottom of each page, later pagination in pencil 305-[278]-583. The numbers in this volume originally started over again, but have been changed to 23-32. At the end of Act Four dated: "21 April 1875" and signed "I:P:E: Hartmann."

titleStmt.title: Arrangement for piano two hands, print, first edition (excerpts)

annot.p: The piano score for "Arcona" started appearing in Horneman & Erslev's periodical "Musikalsk Museum" from July 1875 to February 1877 but was not finished when the periodical discontinued publication. The volumes comprised the following numbers: "Indledning til fjerde Akt"; Finale (transposed from C sharp minor to C minor); "Saxe Lange optegner i sin Celle i Sorø Kloster Minderne fra Hedenold"; "Samtale mellem Esbern og Holdfried"; "Børnenes Dands"; "Festindledning til 2den Act"; and "Narrens Dands".
